oscar: Quick heads-up 3 I opened a small PR to standardize pagination/streaming snippets across py/ts/go. Found several examples still using `page_token` and `page_size`. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4405

priya: I'll take Python. Which tests are failing? docs-ci flagged snippet-tests for formatting and param names.

luke: Go iterator needs a tiny refactor: `Stream()` -> `StreamMessages` and we should document the trailing-empty-page behavior. I've sketched a DropEmptyPages helper.

hannah: TS: will swap the old retry middleware for `withRetries(...)` and show async iterator streaming + a paginated example. Also add `@sdk:2.1.0` in captions.

oscar: Mini checklist: 1) update code samples, 2) include a 1-2 line migration note, 3) add a tiny compile/test snippet, 4) run docs-ci preview.

priya: Python snippet patch (example):
```python
# old
for page in client.paginate_responses(model="x", page_token=resp.next_token):
    process(page)

# new
for page in client.paginate(model="x", cursor=resp.cursor, limit=100):
    process(page)
```

luke: Go helper added under `examples/go/helpers.go` and a test `examples/go/stream_test.go` that asserts helper removes empty pages. Branch: docs/go/4407. PTAL.

hannah: TS preview built: https://deploy-preview.docs.redwood/4405-ts (status: success). Replaced retry example with `withRetries({ retries: 3 })`.

oscar: After merges, we'll backport a short compatibility note to the v1-compat page and add an algolia search alias mapping `page_token` -> `cursor`.

priya: Pushed Python PR `docs/py/paginate-4406`. CI passed after fixing a small fenced code indent.

luke: Go PR opened and tests pass locally. I'll push CI fix for module path.

hannah: Merged TS and updated release-notes draft under "Docs": "Snippets: unified pagination/streaming (cursor/limit), added DropEmptyPages helper, examples target SDK >= 2.1.0."

docs-bot: deploy previews built: 4405, 4406, 4407 (all green) :white_check_mark:

oscar: Nice work. Follow-ups: sweep repo for `page_token`/`page_size`, add small migration snippet for v1 users, and notify support/docs-changelog once backports are live. Thanks :thumbsup:
